Le périmètre ne contient que deux cadres, tous deux sur la page « Intégrations » (cadres-html) : <iframe src="/embed/disponibilite.html"> et <iframe src="/embed/facturation.html">. Vérification faite dans le DOM capturé (.ultra11y/pages/cadres-html/dom.html:27 et :31) ET dans la source (tests/fixtures/realworld/cadres.html:37 et :41) : aucun des deux ne porte d'attribut title (ni aria-label, ni aria-labelledby) — la note de moisson le confirme (title="" name=""). Un grep de tout le périmètre audité ne trouve pas d'autre <iframe> ni de <frame>. Or le test 2.2.1 ne porte QUE sur « chaque cadre pourvu d'un attribut title » : le sujet du critère est vide, il n'y a aucun titre de cadre dont juger la pertinence. L'absence de titre est un défaut réel, mais il relève du critère 2.1 (« chaque cadre a-t-il un titre de cadre ? »), pas de 2.2 — le compter ici reviendrait à sanctionner deux fois le même manquement.

The gray text is styled for visual presentation, but the information is conveyed by the text content itself ('Facturation à la seconde, sans engagement'), not by the color. The text at line 59 uses color rgb(187,187,187) on background rgb(255,255,255). The computed contrast ratio is approximately 1.8:1. Per test 3.2.1, normal text (16px, not bold) must have at least 4.5:1 contrast. This text fails to meet that requirement with no mechanism for user adjustment provided.

findings.message: Text contrast ratio 1.8:1 is below minimum 4.5:1 for normal text

Le média temporel « journal audio des incidents » n'offre aucune fonctionnalité de contrôle de sa consultation : l'élément <audio> n'a pas d'attribut controls, et aucun bouton lecture / pause / stop ni contrôle du son ne figure ailleurs dans la page (aucun <script> dans le périmètre n'en ajoute — vérifié sur la source tests/fixtures/realworld/medias.html:41 comme sur le DOM capturé). Comme il démarre seul (autoplay), l'utilisateur n'a strictement aucun moyen, ni au clavier ni au pointeur, d'arrêter ou de couper le son. Le minimum exigé par le glossaire « contrôle de la consultation » (lecture, pause ou stop, plus activation/désactivation du son puisque le média a du son) est absent. Correctif : ajouter l'attribut controls et retirer autoplay. Le <video controls> de la même page (ligne 29) satisfait, lui, les tests 4.11.1 à 4.11.3 grâce aux contrôles natifs.

Le son se déclenche automatiquement et rien ne permet de l'interrompre au clavier ni au pointeur. Correctif : ajouter controls (et supprimer autoplay).

Both data tables with titles use the <caption> element to correctly associate their titles programmatically. The caption element is the correct method for associating a title with a table according to test 5.4.1. Both captions are properly contained within the <table> element.

entries.justification: Dix des onze <title> relevés portent un contenu, et chacun satisfait le test 8.6.1 : il permet de retrouver la page dans l'historique ou la liste des onglets. Ils suivent tous le même schéma « sujet de la page — nom du site » (Accueil, Intégrations, Contact et compte, Documents, Médias, Plan du site, Recherche, Tarifs — Orbit, hébergement statique), sont distincts deux à deux, concis, non génériques, et le sujet annoncé correspond bien au contenu de la page (vérifié sur les <h1> correspondants : « Intégrations » pour la page des cadres, « Plan du site », « Tarifs »…). Les deux pages embarquées dans les cadres portent également des titres propres et descriptifs de leur contenu (« Disponibilité des services » pour le tableau de disponibilité, « Facturation » pour le formulaire SIRET). La onzième évidence — <title></title> sur mentions-legales-html:6 — est délibérément exclue de ces citations : une balise <title> vide ne constitue pas un « titre de page » au sens du glossaire RGAA (« contenu de la balise <title> permettant d'identifier de manière claire, concise et unique les contenus/la nature de la page »). Cette page n'« a » donc pas de titre de page et sort du champ de 8.6, qui ne juge que les titres existants ; l'absence est un défaut réel relevant du critère 8.5 (test 8.5.1), où le moteur la rattache déjà.

entries.justification: No <q> or <blockquote> elements are present in any of the audited pages. The evidence list contains headings, lists, and other structural elements but no content marked as citations. Tests 9.4.1 and 9.4.2 specifically require identifying citations visually present in the page and verifying they use the correct elements. Since no citations exist in the captured content, this criterion does not apply to the audited scope.

All meaningful content is present in HTML elements, not dependent on CSS visibility. Examining the DOM structure: headings contain text content, lists contain list items with text, forms contain inputs with labels, tables contain cell content. CSS-generated content (::after with content: 'Nouveau') is decorative. Styled elements like those with color:#bbbbbb have their text in the HTML. When CSS is disabled, this content remains present and accessible. Test 10.2.1 is satisfied.

The HTML source order is logical and coherent. Reading through the DOM in source order produces a comprehensible sequence: skip link, header with navigation, main content (headings and sections in logical order), footer. No CSS reordering via flexbox order properties, CSS Grid placement, or other positioning techniques disrupts this natural reading flow. When CSS is disabled, the content order remains appropriate and comprehensible. Test 10.3.1 is satisfied.

Test 10.4.2 requires that text can be enlarged to 200%. The meta viewport with user-scalable=no directly blocks this capability. Test 10.4.1 requires that text remains present and readable when enlarged. The .entrefilet paragraph fails this because its fixed height (20px) combined with overflow:hidden causes text to disappear when zoom is applied.

findings.message: Meta viewport has user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1, which disables zoom scaling entirely. This prevents users from enlarging text to 200% using the browser's zoom function.

entries.justification: The captured evidence shows one element with explicit CSS color declarations (line 59: color:#bbbbbb; background:#ffffff). Across the styles.json, links and text elements with color declarations consistently include background-color values. The CSS structure shows proper pairing of foreground and background colors. Tests 10.5.1 and 10.5.2 are satisfied.

findings.message: Links inside list items have no underline (text-decoration: none) and no explicit hover/focus states. Combined with global focus outline removal (line 59), links are distinguished by color only without required visual feedback at hover or focus.

entries.justification: The test 10.8.1 requires that hidden content either has a vocation to be ignored by assistive technologies OR is made available through user action. The button at line 145 is aria-hidden but visible and focusable to keyboard users, violating the coherence requirement. Bouton radio dont l'étiquette « Oui » est placée visuellement à GAUCHE du champ. La géométrie mesurée sur la capture rendue (boxes.json de contact-html) donne le <label for="rappel-oui"> à x=16..41, y=702 et le bouton radio à x=50, y=704 : même ligne, étiquette avant le contrôle. Aucun des cas particuliers du critère ne s'applique : la page est intégralement en français (sens de lecture unique), les radios sont rendus en boutons radio natifs (13×13 px), et rien dans ce couple oui/non ne justifie une disposition dérogatoire. La conséquence est réelle : la séquence rendue « Oui ◯ Non ◯ » laisse penser que le radio suit l'étiquette qu'il précède. Correctif : placer chaque <label> après son <input type="radio">.

Même défaut sur le second radio du couple : <label for="rappel-non"> mesuré à x=70..100, y=702 et le bouton radio à x=109, y=704 — étiquette à gauche du champ, alors que le test 11.4.3 impose au-dessous ou à droite pour un champ de type radio en lecture gauche-droite.

entries.justification: The page set contains two distinct navigation systems satisfying test 12.1.1. First, a navigation principale menu appears in the header across all pages (evident in all captured pages' `<nav aria-label="Navigation principale">` elements). Second, a dedicated sitemap page exists at /plan.html with title 'Plan du site' listing pages in organized sections. These two systems (menu + sitemap) satisfy the criterion's requirement: 'Un menu de navigation et un plan du site sont présents'.

Test 12.2.1 requires navigation to be in the same place visually and in the same order in the source across pages in a page set. Evidence shows consistent positioning: the header element with navigation principale appears at the start of body on all inspected pages (cadres-html, contact-html, documents-html, medias-html, plan-html, tarifs-html). The navigation structure (`<header><nav aria-label="Navigation principale"><ul><li><a>...`) is identical across pages. While some pages show fewer navigation links (filtered by page relevance), the structural order within the DOM remains consistent: the menu always appears in header before main content. The footer navigation also maintains consistent positioning across pages.

findings.message: The sitemap page (plan-html) has no footer navigation containing a 'Plan du site' link. Footer only contains audio and copyright, making sitemap inaccessible from its own page via the same functionality used on other pages.

The search results page (recherche-html) has no footer navigation containing 'Plan du site' link. The sitemap is not accessible from this page via the same functionality as it is from contact and tarifs pages.
The home page footer contains no navigation landmark linking to the sitemap. Other pages consistently provide 'Plan du site' link in footer navigation, but this page breaks the pattern.

The contact page does not provide access to the search engine from header, footer, or any consistent interface element. The search form exists only on dedicated recherche.html page, not accessible identically from this page.
The sitemap page navigation does not include link to search page. Navigation links in header lack 'Recherche' reference, and no search functionality appears on this page.

The documents page is missing a <main> landmark element entirely. The h1 'Documents à télécharger' starts at line 22 without a containing main element, making the primary content zone not identifiable or reachable via landmark navigation.

The plan du site page contains two <main> landmark elements (at lines 22 and 57). Only one main landmark is allowed per page. Multiple main landmarks violate the requirement that the main content zone be uniquely identified and reachable.

An unnamed <nav> element appears on the plan page at line 29. When multiple navigation landmarks exist, each must have distinguishing aria-label or aria-labelledby. This unnamed navigation cannot be distinguished from the named 'Navigation principale' nav, violating test 12.6.1.

The header contains 9 navigation links (Accueil, Tarifs, Contact, Médias, Intégrations, Documents, Recherche, Plan du site, Mentions légales) in plain links without <nav> landmark. Navigation links should be grouped within <nav> element to identify them as navigation zone for test 12.6.1.

The skip link targets href="#principal" but the main content zone is identified as id="contenu" (line 24). The skip link target does not exist, making it non-functional. Test 12.7.1 requires a functional skip link to the main content zone.

The button has tabindex="1" while the preceding input field has tabindex="3". This causes the button to receive focus before the input field, violating the natural reading order of the form. Test 12.8.1 requires tabulation order to remain coherent with content order.

The input field traps keyboard focus by preventing the Tab key and refocusing itself. The onkeydown handler executes event.preventDefault() when the Tab key is pressed, preventing users from navigating to the next focusable element. Test 12.9.1 requires users to be able to move to the next or previous focusable element or be informed of an alternative mechanism.

entries.justification: The captured evidence concerns a div element with an onclick handler, which is a simple pointer interaction (single-point tap/click). Test 13.10.1 applies to multipoint contact (e.g., pinch gestures, two-finger taps) and test 13.10.2 applies to trajectory-based gestures (e.g., following a drawn path). A simple tap is neither multipoint nor trajectory-based, so these tests do not apply to the evidence provided.

The div element carries an inline onclick handler which, by standard HTML/JavaScript behavior, triggers on the 'click' event. The 'click' event is fired when the pointer is released (not pressed). This means users can move the pointer away from the element before releasing to cancel the action. Test 13.11.1 condition 1 states 'The action is triggered when the pointer is released', which is satisfied by this standard click event behavior, allowing the action to be cancelled by moving away before release.

The evidence presents a div with an onclick handler for a simple pointer interaction. Tests 13.12.1 and 13.12.2 concern functionalities available through device motion (motion sensors like accelerometers) or gestures directed toward the device. No evidence of device motion APIs (devicemotion, deviceorientation, etc.) was found in the audited scope. Since no device motion functionality exists to test, this criterion does not apply.
